title.en: God's plan: all things in Christ
title.zh: 神的計劃：萬有都在基督裏

en: Paul blesses God, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing.
God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world and destined us to be his children.
In Christ we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our wrongdoings.
God has made known the mystery of his will: to bring all things together under one head in Christ.
Christ is the image of the invisible God; all things were created through him and for him.
He is before all things, and he is the head of the body, the church.
Through the blood of his cross God reconciles all things to himself.
zh: 保羅頌讚神，因神在基督裏把天上各樣屬靈的福氣賜給我們。
神在創立世界以前，就在基督裏揀選了我們，預定我們作他的兒女。
我們在基督裏藉着他的血得蒙救贖，過犯得到赦免。
神叫我們知道他旨意的奧祕：要使萬有都在基督裏同歸於一。
基督是那看不見的神的形像，萬有都是藉着他、為着他而造的。
他在萬有之先，也是身體的頭，這身體就是教會。
神藉着基督在十字架上所流的血，使萬有與自己和好。

about.en: All things came into being through the Word
about.zh: 萬物都是藉着道造的

about.en: God has spoken through his Son, heir of all things
about.zh: 神藉着承受萬有的兒子說話

about.en: A new heaven and a new earth
about.zh: 新天新地

en: Ephesus was a great port city of the Roman province of Asia; its ruins lie near Selçuk in western Turkey.
Colossae was a town in the Lycus valley of western Turkey; its site is an unexcavated mound near Honaz.
Paul wrote both letters as a prisoner (Eph 3:1; Col 4:18), traditionally from Rome about AD 60–62.
zh: 以弗所是羅馬亞細亞省的大港口城市，遺址在今土耳其西部的塞爾丘克附近。
歌羅西是土耳其西部呂刻斯河谷的一個城鎮，遺址是霍納茲附近一座尚未發掘的土丘。
保羅寫這兩封信時正被囚禁（以弗所書3章1節；歌羅西書4章18節），傳統認為約在公元60至62年寫於羅馬。

en: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth; the earth was formless and empty.
Day one: God says, "Let there be light." Day two: he makes the dome of the sky.
Day three: dry land and seas appear, and the land produces plants and fruit trees.
Day four: God makes the sun, the moon and the stars. Day five: sea creatures and birds.
Day six: God makes the animals, and then human beings in his image, male and female.
God sees everything he has made, and it is very good.
On the seventh day God rests, and he blesses that day and makes it holy.
zh: 起初，神創造天地；地是荒涼空虛的。
第一日，神說：「要有光。」第二日，他造了天空的穹蒼。
第三日，旱地和海出現，地上長出植物和結果子的樹。
第四日，神造了太陽、月亮和星星。第五日，造了海裏的生物和飛鳥。
第六日，神造了野獸，然後照着自己的形像造人，造男造女。
神看他所造的一切都非常好。
第七日神安息了，他賜福給這一日，定為聖日。

about.en: In the beginning was the Word
about.zh: 太初有道

about.en: By the word of the LORD the heavens were made
about.zh: 諸天藉耶和華的話而造

about.en: The universe was formed by the word of God
about.zh: 宇宙是藉神的話造成的

en: Other ancient peoples told creation stories too; the Babylonian Enuma Elish is known from clay tablets found at Nineveh in the 1800s.
The Hebrew word for the "dome" of the sky means something hammered out or spread out, like beaten metal.
A seven-day week with a day of rest became a mark of Israel; the Romans later adopted the seven-day week.
zh: 其他古代民族也有創世故事；巴比倫的《埃努瑪‧埃利什》見於十九世紀在尼尼微出土的泥版。
希伯來文中天空的「穹蒼」一詞，意思是錘打出來或鋪展開來的東西，像打薄的金屬。
七日一週並有一日安息，成了以色列的特色；後來羅馬人也採用了七日一週。

en: The LORD God forms the man from the dust of the ground and breathes into him the breath of life.
He plants a garden in Eden, with the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flows out of Eden and divides into four, among them the Tigris and the Euphrates.
God puts the man in the garden to work it, and forbids him to eat from the tree of knowledge.
God says it is not good for the man to be alone; the man names all the animals.
God makes the man sleep, takes one of his ribs, and builds it into a woman.
The man says, "Bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh"; the two become one flesh.
zh: 耶和華神用地上的塵土造人，將生命的氣息吹進他的鼻孔。
他在伊甸開闢了一個園子，園中有生命樹和分辨善惡的樹。
有河從伊甸流出，分為四道，其中有希底結和伯拉河。
神把那人安置在園中耕種看守，又吩咐他不可吃分辨善惡樹上的果子。
神說那人獨居不好；那人給所有的動物起名。
神使那人沉睡，取下他的一根肋骨，造成一個女人。
那人說：「這是我骨中的骨，肉中的肉。」二人成為一體。

about.en: Jesus quotes Genesis on marriage
about.zh: 耶穌引用創世記論婚姻

about.en: The first man Adam and the last Adam
about.zh: 首先的亞當和末後的亞當

about.en: What is a human being, that you remember him?
about.zh: 人算甚麼，你竟顧念他

en: The Tigris and Euphrates rise in eastern Turkey and flow through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf; the Pishon and Gihon are not certainly identified.
In Hebrew the word for "man" (adam) sounds like the word for "ground" (adamah).
zh: 希底結河和伯拉河（底格里斯河和幼發拉底河）發源於土耳其東部，流經敘利亞和伊拉克，注入波斯灣；比遜河和基訓河的位置不能確定。
在希伯來文中，「人」（adam）和「地」（adamah）兩個字發音相近。

title.en: The garden of Eden and the fall

en: The snake asks the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree'?"
The snake says, "You will certainly not die," and that she will be like God.
The woman eats the fruit and gives some to her husband, and he eats.
Their eyes are opened; they sew fig leaves together and hide from the LORD God.
God calls, "Where are you?" The man blames the woman, and the woman blames the snake.
God pronounces curses on the snake and the ground, and pain for the woman and the man.
God clothes them with skins and sends them out of Eden; cherubim guard the tree of life.
zh: 蛇問女人：「神真的說過『你們不可吃園中任何樹上的果子』嗎？」
蛇說：「你們一定不會死。」又說她會像神一樣。
女人吃了果子，又給她丈夫，他也吃了。
他們的眼睛開了，就用無花果樹的葉子編裙子，躲避耶和華神。
神呼喚：「你在哪裏？」那人怪女人，女人怪蛇。
神宣告蛇和地受咒詛，女人和男人要受苦楚。
神用皮子給他們做衣服，把他們趕出伊甸；基路伯把守生命樹的路。

about.en: Sin entered the world through one man
about.zh: 罪是從一人入了世界

about.en: The snake deceived Eve by its craftiness
about.zh: 蛇用詭詐誘惑了夏娃

about.en: The tree of life, and no more curse
about.zh: 生命樹，再沒有咒詛

en: Winged guardian figures stood at palace and temple doors in the ancient Near East; cherubim were later carved on the cover of the ark (Exod 25:18–20).
Fig trees grow throughout the Middle East; their leaves are large, as wide as a hand or more.
zh: 古代近東的宮殿和廟宇門口常立有帶翅膀的守衛像；後來約櫃的蓋上也造了基路伯（出埃及記25章18至20節）。
無花果樹遍佈中東各地，葉子很大，有手掌那麼寬或更寬。

en: The LORD God tells the snake that it is cursed and will crawl on its belly.
God will put hostility between the snake and the woman, and between their offspring.
God says of her offspring, "He will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."
Paul writes that when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.
God sent him to redeem those under the Law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
zh: 耶和華神對蛇說，牠必受咒詛，要用肚子爬行。
神要叫蛇和女人彼此為仇，蛇的後代和女人的後代也彼此為仇。
神論到女人的後代說：「他要打傷你的頭，你要打傷他的腳跟。」
保羅寫道，到了時候滿足，神就差遣他的兒子，為女子所生。
神差他來，要救贖律法以下的人，叫我們得着兒子的名分。

about.en: God will soon crush Satan under your feet
about.zh: 神快要將撒但踐踏在你們腳下

about.en: Through his death he broke the power of the one who holds death
about.zh: 他藉着死敗壞掌死權的

about.en: That ancient serpent, called the devil and Satan
about.zh: 古蛇，名叫魔鬼，又叫撒但

en: Early Christian writers, such as Irenaeus about AD 180, read Genesis 3:15 as a first announcement of the gospel; it was later called the "first gospel".
Galatia was a Roman province in central Asia Minor, around modern Ankara in Turkey.
zh: 早期基督徒作者，如約公元180年的愛任紐，把創世記3章15節讀作福音的第一次宣告；後來這節被稱為「原始福音」。
加拉太是羅馬在小亞細亞中部的一個省，在今土耳其的安卡拉一帶。

en: Eve gives birth to Cain and then Abel; Abel keeps flocks and Cain works the ground.
Both bring offerings; the LORD looks with favor on Abel's offering but not on Cain's.
The LORD warns the angry Cain that sin is crouching at the door.
Cain attacks his brother Abel in the field and kills him.
God asks, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain answers, "Am I my brother's keeper?"
Cain is cursed to wander; the LORD puts a mark on him so no one will kill him.
Eve gives birth to Seth in place of Abel, and people begin to call on the name of the LORD.
zh: 夏娃生了該隱，又生了亞伯；亞伯牧羊，該隱耕地。
兩人都獻上供物；耶和華看中了亞伯的供物，卻沒有看中該隱的。
耶和華警告發怒的該隱：罪就伏在門前。
該隱在田間攻擊他的弟弟亞伯，把他殺了。
神問：「你弟弟亞伯在哪裏？」該隱回答：「我豈是看守我弟弟的嗎？」
該隱受咒詛，要流離飄蕩；耶和華給他一個記號，免得人殺他。
夏娃生了塞特代替亞伯；那時人開始求告耶和華的名。

about.en: By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice
about.zh: 亞伯因着信獻上更美的祭

about.en: Do not be like Cain, who killed his brother
about.zh: 不可像殺弟弟的該隱

about.en: Jesus' blood speaks better than Abel's
about.zh: 耶穌的血比亞伯的血所說的更美

en: Farming and herding began in the Fertile Crescent of the Middle East about 10,000 years ago.
Bronze tools came into use in the Near East about 3300 BC; iron became common only after about 1200 BC.
zh: 農耕和畜牧約在一萬年前起源於中東的肥沃月灣。
近東約在公元前3300年開始使用銅器；鐵器要到約公元前1200年以後才普遍。

title.en: Evil on the earth; Noah builds the ark
title.zh: 地上的罪惡；挪亞造方舟

en: The LORD sees that the thoughts of human hearts are only evil all the time, and he is grieved.
But Noah finds favor with the LORD; he is righteous and walks with God.
Noah has three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. The earth is filled with violence.
God tells Noah to build an ark of gopher wood, 300 cubits long, covered with pitch.
God will bring a flood, but he will make his covenant with Noah and his family.
Noah is to bring two of every kind of animal into the ark, and food for all.
Noah does everything just as God commanded him.
zh: 耶和華看見人心裏所想的盡都是惡，就心中憂傷。
惟有挪亞在耶和華眼前蒙恩；他是義人，與神同行。
挪亞有三個兒子：閃、含和雅弗。地上滿了強暴。
神吩咐挪亞用歌斐木造一艘方舟，長三百肘，裏外塗上瀝青。
神要使洪水氾濫，但要與挪亞和他的家人立約。
挪亞要把各樣動物每種兩隻帶進方舟，又要預備眾生的食物。
挪亞照着神吩咐他的一切去做了。

about.en: By faith Noah built an ark
about.zh: 挪亞因着信造了方舟

about.en: As in the days of Noah
about.zh: 挪亞的日子怎樣

about.en: Noah, a herald of righteousness
about.zh: 傳義道的挪亞

en: A cubit was the length of a forearm, about 45 cm (18 in); the ark was about 135 m long, 22 m wide and 13 m high.
Mesopotamian flood stories are found in the Epic of Gilgamesh; George Smith published a flood tablet from Nineveh in 1872.
Pitch (bitumen) seeps from the ground in Mesopotamia and was used there to waterproof boats and baskets.
zh: 一肘是前臂的長度，約45公分；方舟約長135公尺，寬22公尺，高13公尺。
美索不達米亞的洪水故事見於《吉爾伽美什史詩》；1872年喬治‧史密斯發表了尼尼微出土的洪水泥版。
美索不達米亞地下有瀝青滲出，當地人用它塗抹船隻和籃子防水。

title.en: The flood; Noah sends the dove

en: Noah, his family and the animals go into the ark, and the LORD shuts him in.
Rain falls forty days and forty nights; the waters cover the high mountains.
Every living thing on dry land dies; only Noah and those with him are left.
God remembers Noah; the waters go down, and the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat.
Noah sends out a raven, then a dove; the dove returns with an olive leaf, then stays away.
Noah comes out of the ark and offers burnt offerings to the LORD on an altar.
The LORD says that as long as the earth lasts, seedtime and harvest will not cease.
zh: 挪亞、他的家人和動物都進了方舟，耶和華把他關在裏頭。
大雨降在地上四十晝夜；水淹沒了高山。
旱地上一切有生命的都死了；只留下挪亞和與他同在方舟裏的。
神記念挪亞；水漸漸退去，方舟停在亞拉臘的山上。
挪亞放出一隻烏鴉，又放出鴿子；鴿子叼回一片橄欖葉，後來就不再回來。
挪亞出了方舟，在壇上向耶和華獻燔祭。
耶和華說，地還存留的時候，稼穡和收割永不停息。

about.en: The flood came and destroyed them all
about.zh: 洪水來了，把他們全都滅了

about.en: Eight people brought safely through water
about.zh: 八個人藉着水得救

about.en: As I swore the waters of Noah would not return
about.zh: 我曾起誓挪亞的洪水不再漫過

en: Ararat is the ancient kingdom of Urartu, around Lake Van in eastern Turkey and Armenia; the text says only "the mountains of Ararat".
The peak now called Mount Ararat, in eastern Turkey, rises about 5,137 m and is traditionally named as the ark's resting place.
In the Gilgamesh flood story the hero also sends out birds: a dove, a swallow and a raven.
zh: 亞拉臘就是古代的烏拉爾圖王國，在今土耳其東部和亞美尼亞的凡湖一帶；經文只說「亞拉臘的山」。
今天稱為亞拉臘山的山峰在土耳其東部，高約5137公尺，傳統上被認為是方舟停靠之處。
在《吉爾伽美什史詩》的洪水故事裏，主角也放出了鳥：一隻鴿子、一隻燕子和一隻烏鴉。

en: God blesses Noah and his sons: "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth."
Every moving thing will be food for them, but they must not eat meat with its blood.
Whoever sheds human blood will have his own blood shed, for God made humankind in his image.
God makes his covenant with Noah, his offspring and every living creature.
Never again will a flood destroy the earth.
God sets his bow in the clouds as the sign of the covenant, and he will remember it.
zh: 神賜福給挪亞和他的兒子們：「你們要生養眾多，遍滿地面。」
凡活着的動物都可以作他們的食物，只是不可吃帶着血的肉。
凡流人血的，他的血也必被人所流，因為神照着自己的形像造人。
神與挪亞、他的後代和一切活物立約。
洪水不再毀滅大地。
神把他的虹放在雲中，作立約的記號，他必記念這約。

about.en: My covenant of peace will not be removed
about.zh: 我平安的約不遷移

about.en: Like a rainbow in the clouds: the glory of the LORD
about.zh: 像雲中的虹，是耶和華的榮耀

about.en: A rainbow around the throne
about.zh: 寶座周圍有虹

en: The Hebrew word for the rainbow (qeshet) is the ordinary word for a warrior's bow.
Ancient covenants were often marked by a sign or witness, such as a heap of stones or a shared meal (Gen 31:44–54).
zh: 希伯來文中「虹」（qeshet）這個字，就是指戰士所用的弓。
古代立約常有記號或見證，例如一堆石頭或一同吃飯（創世記31章44至54節）。

en: The whole earth has one language, and people settle on a plain in the land of Shinar.
They make baked bricks and use tar for mortar.
They say, "Let us build a city with a tower whose top reaches the heavens."
They want to make a name for themselves and not be scattered over the earth.
The LORD comes down to see the city and confuses their language.
The LORD scatters them over the whole earth, and they stop building the city, called Babel.
zh: 那時全地只有一種語言，人們在示拿地的平原住下來。
他們燒製磚塊，用瀝青當灰泥。
他們說：「我們要建造一座城和一座塔，塔頂通天。」
他們要為自己立名，免得分散在全地上。
耶和華降臨，要看那城，就混亂了他們的語言。
耶和華把他們分散到全地上，他們就停工不建那城了；那城名叫巴別。

about.en: Nimrod's kingdom began at Babel in Shinar
about.zh: 寧錄的國起頭在示拿地的巴別

about.en: At Pentecost each hears in his own language
about.zh: 五旬節各人聽見用自己的鄉談說話

about.en: A crowd from every nation and language
about.zh: 從各國各方言來的群眾

en: Shinar is southern Mesopotamia (Babylonia), in modern Iraq; in Hebrew "Babel" is the name of Babylon.
Mesopotamian cities built ziggurats, stepped temple towers of mud brick; the ziggurat of Babylon was about 90 m high.
Stone was scarce in southern Mesopotamia, so builders used baked brick with bitumen as mortar.
zh: 示拿就是美索不達米亞南部（巴比倫尼亞），在今伊拉克；希伯來文的「巴別」就是巴比倫的名字。
美索不達米亞的城市建有塔廟，是用泥磚築成的階梯形廟塔；巴比倫的塔廟高約90公尺。
美索不達米亞南部缺乏石頭，所以建築用燒過的磚，以瀝青作灰泥。

en: Job lives in Uz; he is blameless and upright, with ten children and great wealth.
The Accuser says to the LORD, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?" The LORD allows him to test Job.
In one day raiders, fire and a great wind take Job's animals, his servants and his children.
Job tears his robe and worships: "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away."
The Accuser strikes Job with painful sores from head to foot.
Job's wife says, "Curse God and die!" Job answers, "Shall we accept the good from God, and not the bad?"
Three friends come and sit silently with Job for seven days and seven nights.
zh: 約伯住在烏斯地，完全正直，有十個兒女和極多的財產。
撒但對耶和華說：「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？」耶和華容許他試驗約伯。
一天之內，強盜、天火和狂風奪去了約伯的牲畜、僕人和兒女。
約伯撕裂外袍，俯伏敬拜：「賞賜的是耶和華，收取的也是耶和華。」
撒但擊打約伯，使他從腳掌到頭頂長滿毒瘡。
約伯的妻子說：「你咒詛神，死了吧！」約伯回答：「我們從神手裏得福，不也受禍嗎？」
三個朋友來了，與約伯一同默默坐了七天七夜。

about.en: You have heard of the endurance of Job
about.zh: 你們聽見過約伯的忍耐

about.en: Noah, Daniel and Job named together
about.zh: 挪亞、但以理、約伯並列

about.en: The Accuser stands to accuse; the LORD rebukes him
about.zh: 撒但站着控告，耶和華責備他

en: The land of Uz is not certainly located; it is often placed in or near Edom (Lam 4:21), east and south of the Dead Sea.
The Sabeans came from Sheba in southern Arabia (modern Yemen); the Chaldeans lived in southern Mesopotamia.
The book does not date its story; Job offers sacrifice as head of his family, as the patriarchs did. Scholars differ on when it was written.
zh: 烏斯地的位置不能確定，常被認為在以東境內或附近（耶利米哀歌4章21節），即死海的東面和南面。
示巴人來自阿拉伯半島南部的示巴（今也門）；迦勒底人住在美索不達米亞南部。
本書沒有註明故事的年代；約伯以家長身分獻祭，與先祖時代相似。學者對本書寫成的時間看法不一。

en: The LORD answers Job out of the storm: "Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?"
God asks about the sea, the light, the snow and rain, the stars, and wild animals and birds.
Job answers, "I am of small account; what can I answer you? I put my hand over my mouth."
God speaks of Behemoth and Leviathan, great creatures that only he can master.
Job says, "I had heard of you, but now my eye sees you," and he repents in dust and ashes.
The LORD is angry with Job's three friends; Job prays for them, and God accepts his prayer.
The LORD gives Job twice as much as before, and seven sons and three daughters; he lives 140 more years.
zh: 耶和華從旋風中回答約伯：「我立大地根基的時候，你在哪裏呢？」
神問到海洋、光明、雪雨、星辰，以及野地的走獸和飛鳥。
約伯回答：「我是卑微的，我用甚麼回答你呢？我只好用手摀口。」
神講到比希摩和利維坦，這些巨大的動物只有他能制伏。
約伯說：「我從前風聞有你，現在親眼看見你。」他就在塵土和爐灰中懊悔。
耶和華向約伯的三個朋友發怒；約伯為他們禱告，神悅納了他的禱告。
耶和華加倍賜給約伯，又賜他七個兒子、三個女兒；此後他又活了一百四十年。

about.en: Paul echoes Job: who has given to God first?
about.zh: 保羅引約伯記：誰是先給了神的

about.en: The Lord is full of compassion and mercy
about.zh: 主是滿心憐憫，大有慈悲

about.en: The LORD set the earth on its foundations
about.zh: 耶和華將地立在根基上

en: Many identify Behemoth with the hippopotamus and Leviathan with the crocodile; others take them as great creatures of poetry. Scholars differ.
The qesitah (Job 42:11) was a unit of money of unknown value, also mentioned in Genesis 33:19 and Joshua 24:32.
Job's friends are named from places linked with Edom and Arabia; Teman was a region of Edom, in modern southern Jordan.
zh: 許多人認為比希摩是河馬，利維坦是鱷魚；也有人認為是詩歌中描寫的巨大生物。學者看法不一。
約伯記42章11節的「一塊銀子」原文是qesitah，是一種錢幣單位，價值不詳，也見於創世記33章19節和約書亞記24章32節。
約伯的朋友以地名稱呼，這些地方與以東和阿拉伯有關；提幔是以東的一個地區，在今約旦南部。
